conn.title: Connection
conn.hint: Endpoint, DNS, MTU and keepalive live in the config sent to the device: they only affect configs generated from now on. When the port changes the server listens on the new port immediately; existing devices cannot connect until they install the new config.
conn.block_private: Block internet-enabled devices from reaching private networks
conn.block_private_hint: Prevents leaking into the internal network the server sits on (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x…).
conn.unprofiled_free: Devices without a profile can reach each other
conn.unprofiled_free_hint: Off (recommended): a device without a profile reaches only the server. On: the behaviour of v0.13 and earlier, every such device can reach every device in the VPN.
conn.update_check_hint: When on, GitHub is asked about a new release once a day. No data is sent and nothing is installed automatically. With this and notifications off, Kut makes no outside connections at all.
conn.ipv6_hint: The tunnel carries IPv6 along with IPv4 (private {ula} network). Profile rules apply to IPv6 as well. Existing devices must regenerate their config to use IPv6.
conn.ipv6_no_tools: ip6tables was not found: install it first.
conn.ipv6_route_yes: The server has IPv6 egress: internet-enabled devices reach IPv6 through NAT66.
conn.ipv6_route_no: The server has no default IPv6 route: IPv6 traffic from internet-enabled devices is dropped in the tunnel (no leak).
conn.ipv6_ra: When enabling, Kut sets accept_ra=2 on the default-route interface so the server's own IPv6 connectivity is not broken.

srvlang.title: Server language
srvlang.label: Default language
srvlang.hint: The language of notifications, command-line output and kut doctor. Each account picks its own panel language; the server language is used in the panel only when neither the account's nor the browser's language is known.

tfa.title: Two-factor authentication
tfa.intro: When on, signing in asks for the 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password…) after the password. Even if the password leaks, the panel cannot be entered.
tfa.lost_pre: If you lose your phone, running
tfa.scan: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code from the app.
tfa.manual: If you cannot scan the QR code, enter the key manually:
tfa.rec_warn: These codes are shown only now. Each can be used once; you need them to sign in if you lose your phone. Store them somewhere safe.
tfa.copy_failed: Could not copy; select it manually.

users.title: Accounts
users.intro: An administrator can do everything; a viewer can only look at the panel. Every account has its own password and 2FA. “admin” is the owner account and cannot be deleted.
users.name: Username (lowercase letters, digits, . _ -)
users.edit_hint: When the role or password changes, this account's open sessions are closed.
users.del_confirm: Delete “{name}”? Their open sessions are closed immediately.
